newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil external debt-servicing $20 bln this year.
newsitem.headline: Brazil external debt-servicing $20 bln this year.

text.p: Brazil's public and private sectors will have to come up with $20 billion to service their external debt this year, but those outflows should slow to between $12-13 billion in 1998, a Central Bank official said.

Altamir Lopes, head of the bank's economics department, told Reuters he was not concerned by the size of this year's debt-servicing costs, which have already put pressure on the country's widening current account balance of payments gap.
"The figure this year is high, about $20 billion, but it will come down next year again to about $12-13 billion," Lopes said.
According to Central Bank figures published last week, the public sector will account for $7.198 billion of external debt coming due this year.
That figure rises to $7.509 billion in 1998 and then slips to $6.624 billion in 1999 and $5.284 billion in the year 2000.
Lopes said he could not say exactly how much internal debt would come due this year or next because domestic government securities were often retired early.
He said there were no concerns within the Central Bank about the chronology of internal debt maturities, as the paper could always be rolled over.

Of 152.994 billion reais of Brazilian government securities as of April 1997, the Central Bank has classified 54.7 billion reais in National Treasury Letters (LTNs) and 45.15 billion reais of Central Bank Bonds (BBCs) as short-term debt.

The government's medium-term obligations include 55 million reais in National Treasury Bonds (BTNs), 50.785 billion reais in National Treasury Notes (NTNs) and 2.304 billion reais in Central Bank Notes (NBC-Es).
